comment: Known answers for OWASP Juice Shop. We did not write these down from reading the code and deciding what counts: Juice Shop annotates the exact line of each planted defect in its own source with `// vuln-code-snippet vuln-line <challengeName>`, and `benchmarks/juiceshop.mjs` extracts them. Twenty-seven annotated lines across nine files, grouped here into the sixteen defects they describe. Five of them we do not find, and they are counted in the denominator on purpose: a benchmark you can only pass by removing the questions measures nothing. Each miss names why, and a miss marked `judgement` is a decision not to over-claim rather than a bug to fix.
authored_by: the Juice Shop project, via its own vuln-code-snippet annotations

defects.cause: the administration, score-board, web3-sandbox and token-sale routes are registered with no guard, so the client will render them for anyone who types the path
not_the_cause: the server is still expected to authorize the API calls those pages make
a route being absent from the navigation menu
defects.why_missed: a frontend route without a guard is the normal case — most routes in most applications have none and should not. Which routes need one is a statement about the application, not a pattern in it, so a rule here would report every route in every repository.

defects.cause: bypassSecurityTrustHtml is called on a product description from the API and on the search term from the URL, switching off the escaping that makes XSS rare in Angular
not_the_cause: Angular being insecure by default
a missing Content-Security-Policy, which would reduce the impact and not the defect

defects.cause: the redirect allowlist contains cryptocurrency addresses, so the redirector will happily send a user to one
not_the_cause: the allowlist mechanism itself, which is the right shape
defects.why_missed: whether an entry belongs in an allowlist is a question about the business, not the code. No rule can read that list and know which URL is inappropriate.

defects.cause: the allowlist is enforced with url.includes(allowedUrl), which passes for any URL that merely contains an allowed one anywhere in it
not_the_cause: the allowlist being too short
the redirect endpoint existing at all

defects.cause: the password setter stores security.hash(clearTextPassword), and that helper is crypto.createHash('md5') in lib/insecurity.ts — an unsalted fast digest rather than a key derivation function
not_the_cause: passwords being stored at all
the absence of a password policy, which is a separate control
the setter itself, which names a helper and is the line that shows the defect rather than the line that causes it
defects.was_missed_until: the cross-file check. This defect was recorded as out of reach — the weak primitive is in another module and no regular expression follows a function into another file — and it stayed a miss for one full measurement cycle, which is what put M12 at `failing`. `adapters/scanners/builtin/crossfile.mjs` resolves one hop, and the grade moved because the tool changed, not because the answer did.

defects.cause: the chatbot's coupon tool declares its discount argument as z.number().describe('... maximum 10') — the bound is in a sentence the model reads, not in the schema the server enforces — and the handler mints a coupon for whatever number comes back
not_the_cause: the chatbot being able to issue coupons, which is the feature
the model being badly prompted: a better prompt is still an instruction, and instructions are what prompt injection overrides

defects.cause: the email and the password hash are interpolated into a raw SELECT, so a quote in the email changes the shape of the query and logs in as the first user
not_the_cause: weak password storage
the absence of rate limiting

defects.cause: the search term is interpolated into a raw SELECT, which allows a UNION and with it the whole schema
not_the_cause: the 200-character truncation, which limits the payload and not the defect

defects.cause: the review id comes from the JSON body straight into the filter, so a body can send an operator object instead of a value and the update matches every review
not_the_cause: the multi flag alone, which only decides how many of the matched rows change
SQL injection — this is a document store and the value is the query language

defects.cause: the handler reads the authenticated user and then never uses it in the filter, so any signed-in account can edit any review
not_the_cause: the NoSQL operator issue on the same line, which is a different defect with a different fix
defects.why_missed: `caller-identity-fetched-and-unused` was written for exactly this shape and correctly does not fire here. The handler binds `user` on line 16 and does use it again on line 24 — inside `challengeUtils.solveIf(...)`, Juice Shop's own challenge-tracking scaffolding. Deciding that a use inside solveIf is not an authorization use means knowing what solveIf is for, which is a statement about this application. The check fires where the variable is genuinely never read again, and this is not that; claiming it would mean tuning the rule to one corpus.

defects.cause: serveIndex makes /ftp and /support/logs browsable, which is how the backup and the access log are found
not_the_cause: the files being present on disk, which is expected

defects.cause: the password-reset limiter counts per X-Forwarded-For, a header the client sets, so changing it resets the count
not_the_cause: the limit being too high

defects.cause: the isAuthorized guard on PUT /api/Products/:id is commented out while the neighbouring POST and DELETE keep theirs
not_the_cause: a missing guard — the guard is written, and one character from being live

defects.cause: finale generates CRUD over UserModel with exclude: ['password', 'totpSecret'], and the model declares `role`. The generated POST /api/Users therefore accepts role, so a registration can ask for admin
not_the_cause: the absence of email verification
the create hook on the line the annotation marks, which only creates a wallet
defects.was_missed_until: the cross-file check. Recorded first as judgement — mass assignment is only a defect when an assignable field is privileged, and which one that is depends on the application. That is still true, and it turned out to be readable: the model declares the column and the resource lists its exclusions, so the gap between two lists is the defect. The CWE was re-recorded from CWE-269 to CWE-915, which is the more precise weakness; the original is kept above so the change is visible rather than quietly helpful.

defects.cause: /metrics is registered with no authorization, publishing counters that describe the application and its traffic
not_the_cause: Prometheus metrics being collected at all

accepted_comment: Real findings Juice Shop did not annotate. Its vuln-code-snippet markers cover the lines its challenges are built on, not every defect in the application — it is deliberately vulnerable throughout. Each rule listed here was checked against the source by hand before being accepted; they are not counted as planted, because we did not have a recorded answer for them before the scan.
